entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Leader of the Opposition, a title traditionally held by the leader of the largest party not in government in a Westminster system of parliamentary government, has played a crucial role in shaping the trajectory of modern democracy. 

In the 18th century, the Opposition party in the British Parliament, led by figures such as Charles James Fox and Edmund Burke, played a key role in promoting parliamentary reform and limiting the power of the monarch. 

In the 20th century, the Opposition party in various countries, including India and Australia, has often served as a check on the power of the ruling party, promoting accountability and transparency. 

The legacy of the Leader of the Opposition can be seen in the development of modern parliamentary systems around the world, where the opposition party plays a critical role in holding the government accountable.
